Hi Aditya — thanks for the recap and the demo. Emily and I went through a few follow-up items; attaching our security questionnaire for now. High-level questions below so you can prioritize what to send back: 

1) PII scope: We consider name, date of birth, SSN (very rare), and contact details as regulated. Can you confirm if Redwood has any default redaction or selective masking for these fields at ingestion?

2) Log retention: We need request/response logs retained for 90 days in searchable form, and then moved to an archive for 7 years in case of audit. Are configurable retention windows supported per-tenant?

3) Region pinning vs backups: We require inference to run in US regions only, but we understand backups may cross regions for DR. Is warm-standby in another region an option, and what are the guarantees around data movement during failover?

4) Encryption & keys: Can you confirm support for customer-managed keys (KMS/HSM)? Do backups use the same KMS scope?

5) Audit/log access: What admin roles can export logs? Can we restrict access to a small set of customers’ security contacts?

Please see attached: MedWorks_Security_Questionnaire.pdf (we filled the front half; the rest has vendor evidence requests).

If you prefer, we can hop on a 30-min call with our security lead on Thursday.

Thanks,

Aaron / Emily — looping in the technical details you requested. I’ll keep this high-level and attach links to evidence we can provide.

1) PII ingestion & masking:
- Redwood does not automatically redact user-provided PII at the inference layer by default. We provide pre-processing hooks and an optional input-sanitization library for masking PHI/PII before it reaches the model. That library can be applied per-tenant at the API gateway.
- For higher-assurance workflows we offer a pattern where customer-side middleware performs deterministic tokenization before sending content to Redwood (we can share a reference implementation).

2) Retention & archival:
- Per-tenant configurable retention windows are supported. Default request/response log retention = 30 days. You can configure retention to 90 days (searchable) and then automatic archival to cold storage for longer-term retention (7+ years).
- Archival is encrypted and stored in a region you select; we can pin archival data to the US only.
- We also support on-demand purge APIs to satisfy subject-access requests or DSARs.

3) Region pinning & failover semantics:
- Pinning: you can pin inference and searchable logs to US-only.
- Backups/archives: you can elect to keep backups in US-only or allow cross-region replication.
- Warm-standby: supported. Warm standby means a pre-provisioned pool in a secondary region with data replicated asynchronously — typical RPOs are in the 5–15 minute window depending on workload and batching; RTO for warm-standby is generally sub-30 minutes for small fleets, longer for large committed pools.
- Cold backups (object storage snapshots) have longer RTOs (hours) and are recommended only for long-term archival.

4) Encryption & keys:
- We support customer-managed keys (KMS) for both live data and backups. KMS integration works with major cloud providers; HSM-backed keys are supported for dedicated/private deployments.
- Backups can be encrypted with the same KMS or a separate key per-region per-tenant (configurable).

5) Audit & admin access:
- Admin roles are RBAC-based. Log export and audit access can be restricted to named roles; we can also configure single-signon group mappings to limit access to your security contacts.
- We provide an audit trail with token-level metadata and access logs; these are searchable within your retention window.

Evidence & links:
- SOC2 Type II summary (available on request via secure link)
- Region pinning overview: https://redwood.company/kb/region-pinning-overview
- Reference implementation: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1a2b3-redwood-medworks-ctd

Aaron / Emily — thanks for the detailed questionnaire and Neha for the technical write-up. Quick summary and proposed next steps so nothing falls through the cracks: 

Summary of commitments from Redwood:
- PII handling: provide the input-sanitization library + reference tokenization pattern and an implementation note for ingestion-side masking.
- Retention: support 90-day searchable retention with archival to US-only cold storage for 7 years; automatic purge APIs available for DSARs.
- Failover & backups: offer warm-standby in a secondary US region (typical RTO < 30 min, RPO 5–15 min) and cold backups to object storage for long-term archival.
- Keys & encryption: support customer-managed KMS/HSM; backups can use separate key per-region.
- Audit: RBAC for log exports and a searchable audit trail within retention window.

- Neha: produce a 1-page technical note with the figures above + suggested contract clauses (ETA: EOD Thursday).
